title: Terminal segment-wide operation known controls

target.description: Whether a six-operation segment-wide runtime independently selects and replays the established Page 73 and Page 74 terminal operators

summary: The six-operation family selected the established sequential-prime/totient operator for Page 73 and direct GP for Page 74; both known controls beat 500 full-family shuffles.
why_run: To test whether the segment-wide runtime can recover known terminal material when the correct operator is present before it is used as a negative or discovery instrument.

pipeline.description: Cross-check the retained JSON and CSV ledgers, the selected operation and established text for each terminal segment, separation from the strongest shuffled controls, and the exact empirical p value.

acceptance.criterion: Each established terminal plaintext ranks first under its known operator and exceeds every retained full-family shuffled control in token and vocabulary measures.

output.stdout: PASS — 14/14 E159 terminal-control checks; both established operators separate.

controls: Page 73 and Page 74 are established terminal plaintext controls, not HMS-originated discoveries.
The declared family contains six complete-segment operations and selects the best without resetting at internal red records.
Each terminal control is compared with 500 full-family shuffled inputs using token and vocabulary measures.
The public verifier requires exact JSON/CSV agreement and recomputes p as 1/(500+1).
interpretation: The segment-wide runtime recognizes both known terminal operators when they are in the declared family. This validates the instrument as a control but does not establish an operator for any unsolved segment.
limitations: Both plaintexts and their operations were already known; this is a positive control, not a new translation.
The public package retains the complete terminal-control ledger but not the private typed event streams needed to rerun transformation from source glyphs, so reproduction is PARTIAL.
Success on two terminal controls does not prove that every LP2 segment uses one of the six operations.
This package does not publish the unsolved-segment best-output ledger or forward selector experiments.

normalization_changes: Separated the two known terminal controls from the unsolved-segment scan and later selector work.
Retained the complete terminal full-family control ledger and result object.
Added a portable non-mutating ledger verifier.
Excluded unsolved best outputs, active route detail, private typed event streams, and forward experiments.

raw_artifacts.reason: The terminal known-control result and full-family control ledger are retained; private typed input streams and unsolved-output scans are excluded.
